regions.summary: Upper Zhuozhang River uplands north of Changzhi: Tunliu, Xiangyuan, Wuxiang, Qin county.

candidates.name: Xiangyuan
candidates.meaning: County name from the Warring States, used since 247 BC; the Wikipedia article gives no etymology.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Xiangyuan (25% of the region); the county is among the oldest in the area, with its seat in the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 1267 hits with 山西, top ones about this county.
candidates.source_note: 襄垣县 (县, 247 BC-1911, 2146 yrs) 今山西襄垣县城北关

candidates.name: Zhuozhang
candidates.meaning: "Turbid Zhang": the Zhuozhang River (also called the Lu River), the muddier of the two branches of the Zhang River.
candidates.fit: Both headwater branches run through Wuxiang, Qin county and Xiangyuan, so most of the region is its upper basin; it also runs on through region 3.
candidates.recognisability: Own section in the zh-wiki Zhang River article; only 33 hits with 山西, a river name known mainly locally.
candidates.source_note: 浊漳河（又稱潞水或潞川）流经...

candidates.name: Tunliu
candidates.meaning: From Chunliu, the Jin name for the land of the Liuxu Chidi people; "chun" meant great or fine and is interchangeable with "tun".
candidates.fit: Largest unit (27%), fully inside, but its only a quarter of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article (Tunliu district), well known as a Shangdang county.
candidates.source_note: 屯留县名起源于春秋时期赤狄的支属留吁...晋人改称这里为纯留

regions.notes: Taihang is already on the map to the north-east, so no mountain name here.

regions.summary: Taiyue mountains and the upper Fen valley south of Lingshi: Hongdong, Huozhou, Qinyuan, Fushan, Gu, Anze.

candidates.name: Huozhou
candidates.meaning: Prefecture named for Mount Huo (Huotai Mountain), which rises behind it.
candidates.fit: Holds 93% of Huozhou city (23% of the region); a prefecture seat from 1215, with older Huo prefectures on the same site.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; city of 283k in Kontur cities list.
candidates.source_note: 霍州 (州, 1215-1911) 今山西霍州市

candidates.name: Hongdong
candidates.meaning: County name in use since the Tang (618), seat of the famous Great Locust Tree migration story.
candidates.fit: Largest unit (29%) but the region holds only 44% of the county; the locust tree town and the county seat lie in region 4.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, very widely known nationally.
candidates.source_note: 洪洞县 (县, 618-1911) 今山西洪洞县

regions.notes: Hongdong is better known than Huozhou, but its centre sits in the Linfen region next door.

regions.summary: Shangdang basin around Changzhi's west and east: Huguan, Zhangzi, Lucheng, Licheng, Pingshun, part of Changzhi county.

candidates.name: Zhangzi
candidates.meaning: Warring States county, said to be the home of Danzhu, Yao's eldest son ("changzi").
candidates.fit: Holds 84% of Zhangzi county (21%); seat of the Shangdang commandery for 480 years.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, county of long standing.
candidates.source_note: 上党郡 (郡, 204 BC-353) 今山西长子县城; 长子县 (县, 247 BC-1911)

candidates.name: Shangdang
candidates.meaning: "Upper party": a place so high it stands as a companion to Heaven; the old commandery and region of the Changzhi basin.
candidates.fit: Covers the whole basin; the commandery seat lay at Zhangzi (here) for 480 years, but also at the Changzhi city site for 288 years.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 1194 hits with 山西; also the Shangdang Campaign.
candidates.source_note: 狄子奇《国策地名考》曰：“地极高，与天为党，故曰上党”

candidates.name: Huguan
candidates.meaning: "Pot pass": a pass in the Taihang named for a pot-shaped mountain.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Huguan (21%), joint largest unit with Zhangzi.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; the Huguan Gorge is a national geopark.
candidates.source_note: 壶关县 (县, 489-1911) 今山西壶关县东南

regions.notes: Shangdang also suits region 5 (Changzhi city). I put it here because region 5 gets the prefecture name.

regions.summary: Linfen city centre: Yaodou district and the Dahuaishu part of Hongdong.

candidates.name: Linfen
candidates.meaning: "Beside the Fen": the city on the Fen River; Linfen county existed from 583.
candidates.fit: Holds the old centre of the prefecture seat (74% Yaodou).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; city of 3.9M in the cities list.
candidates.source_note: 临汾县 (县, 583-1911) 今山西临汾市

regions.notes: Region 4 is small (432 px) but it is the city's centre, so it takes the city name.

regions.summary: Changzhi city centre: Cheng district, Jiao district and part of Changzhi county (Shangdang district).

candidates.name: Changzhi
candidates.meaning: "Lasting order": name given to the county in 1529 when Luan Prefecture was set up (Changzhi county from 1529).
candidates.fit: Holds the old city centre; the prefecture seat from 583, and Shangdang commandery seat.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; city of 3.2M in the cities list.

regions.summary: Yellow River bend on the west: Hejin, Jishan, Xiangning, Pu, Ji, Daning.

candidates.name: Hejin
candidates.meaning: "River ford": the Yellow River crossing at the Longmen (Dragon Gate) gorge.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Hejin city (35%), the largest unit, at the foot of the Longmen gorge.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; city of 396k.
candidates.source_note: 龙门郡 (郡, 556-582) 今山西省河津县西阳村乡太阳堡村东

candidates.name: Hukou
candidates.meaning: "Pot mouth": the Hukou Waterfall, where the Yellow River squeezes into a gorge.
candidates.fit: The falls (36.15N 110.44E) lie on the western edge, in Ji county, which holds a tenth of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 413 hits with 山西; one of China's best-known waterfalls.

candidates.name: Jishan
candidates.meaning: Mount Ji, named for Hou Ji, ancestor of agriculture, who legend says taught farming here.
candidates.fit: Holds 74% of Jishan county (24%), second largest unit.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article for the county.
candidates.source_note: 绛州 (州, 577-582) 今山西稷山县西南十二里

regions.notes: Hejin and Jishan are neighbouring county names; Hukou gives a different kind.

regions.summary: Lower Fen valley south of Linfen: Xiangfen, west part of Yaodou, Xinjiang, part of Hongdong.

candidates.name: Taosi
candidates.meaning: Taosi site, a walled Longshan-period city believed to be Yao's capital Pingyang.
candidates.fit: The site is in Xiangfen, 7 km north-east of its seat, the largest unit (35%).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 989 hits with 山西; major early-state archaeological site.
candidates.source_note: 陶寺遺址位於中國山西省襄汾縣城東北七公里的陶寺乡中

candidates.name: Jiangzhou
candidates.meaning: Jiang prefecture, seated at Xinjiang (Baibi village) from 561 for over 1,100 years.
candidates.fit: Seat is in the region (Xinjiang 19%); Jiangzhou's lands also reach Jishan and Yicheng.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 770 hits; Jiangzhou drums and Jiangzhou hall.
candidates.source_note: 绛州 (州/直隶州, 561-1911) 今山西新绛县柏壁村

candidates.name: Xiangfen
candidates.meaning: Formed in 1954 from Xiangling and Taiping counties; "xiang" for the first, "fen" for the Fen River.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Xiangfen (35%).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.

regions.notes: Jiang prefecture and the old Jin capital Jiang overlap region 9's Jiang county only by name.

regions.summary: Northern Jincheng highlands: Gaoping, Yangcheng, Lingchuan, Qinshui, a bit of Zezhou.

candidates.name: Gaoping
candidates.meaning: "High plain"; county from 569, battle site of Changping.
candidates.fit: Holds 88% of Gaoping city (40%), the largest unit; the 40% is by far the biggest.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; city of 485k.
candidates.source_note: 高平县 (县, 569-1911) 今山西高平市区

candidates.name: Changping
candidates.meaning: "Long plain": the Changping commandery seated at Gaoping, scene of the 260 BC Qin-Zhao battle.
candidates.fit: Commandery seat is Gaoping; the battle is tied to the region.
candidates.recognisability: 99 hits with 山西, but the name also points to Changping in Beijing; top hits are about Gaoping.
candidates.source_note: 长平郡 (郡, 529-617) 今山西高平市区

regions.summary: Old Jin heartland between Linfen and Yuncheng: Yicheng, Jiang, Houma, Quwo.

candidates.name: Yicheng
candidates.meaning: "City of Yi": Yi was an early capital of the Jin state.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Yicheng (28%), largest unit.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 翼城县 (县, 598-1911) 今山西翼城东南北绛村

candidates.name: Quwo
candidates.meaning: "Curved fertile land": the base of the Quwo branch that took over Jin.
candidates.fit: Holds all of Quwo county (19%).
candidates.recognisability: Quwo's own county; no standalone article in sources, so the name is checked only through Jin history.
candidates.source_note: 曲沃县 (县, 590-1911) 今山西曲沃县城

candidates.name: Houma
candidates.meaning: "Marquis's horse": a Jin capital Xintian lay here; site of the Houma Covenant tablets.
candidates.fit: Holds 98% of the city (22%).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 侯马市, 新田乡

regions.notes: Yicheng and Quwo are the two rival Jin seats, a pair that works well on adjacent regions if the neighbour is also named.

regions.summary: Jincheng city centre: Cheng district and Zezhou county.

candidates.name: Jincheng
candidates.meaning: "Jin city": Jincheng county from 620, prefecture seat for centuries.
candidates.fit: Holds the old centre (Cheng district 55%).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article; city of 2.3M in the cities list.
candidates.source_note: 晋城县 (县, 620-1367) 今山西晋城市

candidates.name: Zezhou
candidates.meaning: "Marsh prefecture": prefecture of 583-1727 and Zezhou fu to 1911.
candidates.fit: Seat was at Gaodu in today's Zezhou county (37% of the region).
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 泽州 (州, 583-1727) 今山西泽州县高都村

regions.summary: Zhongtiao mountains and the Yellow River bend: Wenxi, Xia, Yuanqu, Wanrong.

candidates.name: Zhongtiao
candidates.meaning: The Zhongtiao range: a long narrow ridge between the Qinling and Taihang, bordering the Yellow River.
candidates.fit: Wenxi, Xia and Yuanqu (the three main units, 74%) lie on its northern and eastern slopes.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 233 hits with 山西; the Zhongtiao Mountain Campaign.
candidates.source_note: 中条山，中国山西省南部主要山脉之一

candidates.name: Wenxi
candidates.meaning: "Heard joy": Emperor Wu of Han is said to have heard news of victory here in 111 BC.
candidates.fit: Holds 92% of Wenxi (32%), the largest unit.
candidates.recognisability: County with 1,966 years of history, home of the Pei family.
candidates.source_note: 闻喜县 (县, 111 BC-1911) 今山西闻喜县西南

candidates.name: Xia
candidates.meaning: Xia county, linked to the first dynasty, Xia, whose capital Anyi tradition places at Xia county.
candidates.fit: Holds 78% of Xia county (23%).
candidates.recognisability: The single character is the name of the dynasty; a lone "Xia" may be confused with the dynasty or Xiamen.
candidates.source_note: 夏县 (县, 494-1911) 今山西夏县禹王乡

regions.summary: Yellow River plain at the south-west corner: Linyi, Yongji, Wanrong.

candidates.name: Puzhou
candidates.meaning: "Cattail prefecture": the old Hedong seat at the Yellow River ferry, now a town in Yongji.
candidates.fit: Puzhou is in Yongji, 33% of the region, on its south-west edge.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 1216 hits with 山西, top ones about people from Pu prefecture.
candidates.source_note: 蒲州 (州, 618-619) 今山西临猗县临晋镇附近; 蒲坂县 今山西永济县西南蒲州镇东

candidates.name: Yongji
candidates.meaning: "Lasting relief"; the county-level city that grew out of the old Puzhou area.
candidates.fit: Holds 87% of Yongji city (33%); city of 445k.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 永济市

candidates.name: Linyi
candidates.meaning: "Beside Yi": Linyi county, from Linjin plus Yishi.
candidates.fit: Largest unit (44%).
candidates.recognisability: Same pinyin as the 11M city Linyi in Shandong, so confusing.
candidates.source_note: 临猗县

regions.summary: Yuncheng city centre: Yanhu district around the Salt Lake.

candidates.name: Yuncheng
candidates.meaning: "Transport city": from the salt transport depot of the Salt Lake.
candidates.fit: Holds the city centre (Yanhu 87%); prefecture name, city of 4.8M for the prefecture.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 运城市

candidates.name: Yanhu
candidates.meaning: "Salt lake": the district named for the Yuncheng Salt Lake.
candidates.fit: 87% of the region, but the prefecture name goes to the central region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article.
candidates.source_note: 盐湖区
